name: Task-proportional choice of interruption surface
summary: A dialog is considered for a bounded interrupting task; inline feedback, disclosure or a full page remains an explicit alternative when no deliberate interruption is justified.
problem: An interface may turn routine field feedback or an extended multistep process into a floating interruption, separating content and actions from context.
context: Task-design decision before selecting a container for confirmations, acknowledgments, short selections, supplementary messages or long structured workflows.
observed_solution: USWDS and Primer Product both discuss dialogs for transient focused tasks and recommend alternatives when longer complexity, field errors or oversized content would be better served inline or on a page; APG disclosure and native HTML nonmodal presentation are distinct interaction models, not interchangeable dialogs.
rationale: W07-O19 and O23 supply USWDS interruption/countercontext/mobile-scroll guidance; O25 supplies Primer Product transient task/size/full-page warning; O18 describes disclosure's button-controlled reveal; O07 and O11 delimit native dialog/popover as different mechanisms. C1 A/E and disputes C03, C12, C16 show compatible contextual design advice, NOT a measured completion-rate benefit, a normative component chooser, or proof of native implementation equivalence. W07-S4 and S5 are unpinned product docs from different design systems, not measured trials.
tradeoffs: An explicit confirmation dialog may reduce accidental commitment in consequential workflows but interrupts continuity; neither risk reduction nor completion-rate impact was measured.
A dedicated page can preserve long semantics and multiple steps yet adds navigation context and may be excessive for a short transient choice.
An inline/disclosure alternative preserves page context but might lack a warranted interruption for an actual required acknowledgment.
applicability: Short, user-triggered confirmations or selections with a bounded decision and intelligible continuation path.
Early design choice where lengthy structured content, page-level status, or field-local feedback competes with a proposed dialog.
non_applicability: A product or legal requirement for an explicit acknowledgment is not disproven by a generic last-resort warning; actual choice/exit mechanics require task authority.
A native platform dialog, nonmodal popover and APG disclosure do not share the same lifecycle; this candidate does not prescribe switching one for another without a semantics review.
No universal pixel width, mobile breakpoint, interruption threshold or framework API is inferred.
accessibility_implications: If a modal is chosen, assess truthful modality, accessible purpose, keyboard exit and focus using applicable WCAG criteria and APG guidance; O01–O05/O13–O16 and C1 B remain context-dependent.
The choice of container alone does not prove keyboard, AT, screen-reader or zoom conformance; no such tests ran.
performance_implications: No comparative render, hydration, memory, animation or responsiveness measurement exists; performance tradeoff UNKNOWN.
responsive_implications: O23/O25 warn that long content and offscreen actions may warrant a dedicated page or more suitable surface; no tested responsive layout or width bound.
implementation_notes: K5 candidate, not a library/component recommendation; design-system named sizes and class/API conventions are not generic requirements.
C1 C03/C12 classify native HTML dialogs/popovers and design-system overlays as not mechanically comparable.
Source rights for USWDS/Primer Product docs remain UNKNOWN; descriptions are source-linked original paraphrases, not copied implementation material.
Original WHATWG source is living/unpinned; do not assert native algorithm behavior for an untested target browser.

counterexamples.summary: USWDS required acknowledgment can intentionally retain the interruption until an explicit choice is made.
counterexamples.context: Time-sensitive or required task gate with a clear path to accept or reject, subject to accessibility and task review.

counterexamples.summary: Large dialog content can be presented in a dialog variant, but Primer asks whether a dedicated page is more appropriate.
counterexamples.context: A transient form or selection with justified constrained size rather than an extensive multistep flow.

version_context: USWDS Modal and Primer Product Dialog live/unpinned 2026-10-08/09; WAI APG explanatory unpinned; WHATWG living HTML 2026-10-08; WCAG criteria relevant only in their actual scopes.
